text.text_excerpt: First, let me say a few words regarding the negative reviews. I think, for the most part, those writing these reviews just don't get it, or maybe even don't get New Orleans. This place is a time-warp, and an endangered species. I can understand that some people do not like old-school places like Dempsey's- I would suggest that you just don't go if you're built that way. Now, to the reviewers who felt they didn't get quality food: I really question that sentiment, having been a regular here for at least 20 years. In those 20 years, I've never had a meal that wasn't at least above-average, and I can be highly critical. I'll be the first to bitch the second Dempsey's lets me down, but 20 yea...

Pretty much the greatest. I'd lived around the corner from this place for about a year before I set foot in it. As a vegetarian, seafood places are usually pretty low on my list of fooderies. However, I had an old friend in town and he wanted to try some New Orleans seafood. We'd made plans to hit Deanie's, but after a long day of abusing drugs and cavorting in the summer hell heat that is August in New Orleans, we decided to keep it in the neighborhood. Christ, this place is a hidden gem. The inside reminds me of the bar my dad got stoned in with his buddies post weird middle-aged dude softball league games when I was a kid, circa 1995. The only real difference is these people can fuckin...

Walking by the neighborhood and my hubby and I decided to try this restaurant and boy they have one of the best fried catfish and soft shell crab I've ever had in my life both are well seasoned and doesn't have that fishy taste. Their char broiled oysters are AMAZING, tangy, sweet and cheesy and the crab balls are delicious as well. We definitely be back again and try other food on their menu. :)
